story.summaryZh: 维斯塔潘表示红牛急需弄清赛车为何有时会在一个F1周末中越跑越差，技术总监瓦什则指出小红牛22还存在入弯稳定性和弯中转向不足两大弱点。

story.summaryEn: Max Verstappen says Red Bull urgently needs to understand why its car sometimes gets worse over the course of an F1 weekend, while technical director Pierre Wache points to entry stability and mid-corner understeer as two weaknesses of the RB22.
detailZh: 维斯塔潘强调红牛在2026赛季F1下半程的“首要任务”
马克斯·维斯塔潘表示，红牛迫切需要弄清为什么其赛车有时会在一个F1周末的进程中越跑越差。技术总监皮埃尔·瓦什则指出了另一个弱点。
在F1夏休期间，马克斯·维斯塔潘落后积分榜领先者基米·安东内利多达110分。
上赛季，这位四届世界冠军从赞德沃特开始发起惊人反击，下半赛季每场大奖赛都登上领奖台，但这次他完全不期待那种情况。
红牛这次的问题更为复杂。车队赛季初就带着明显劣势起步，这在意料之中，尽管原因不同。赛季前，其自家动力单元是最大的问号，不过DM01已被证明出人意料地有竞争力。
然而在底盘方面，短板更大。再加上小红牛22的超重问题，就能明白为何根据Paceteq的数据，红牛在澳大利亚和中国纯比赛节奏上落后超过1.3秒。
在比利时和匈牙利，这一差距已缩小到每圈两成，不过维斯塔潘认为这些数字并不能说明全部情况。
在布达佩斯，这位荷兰人表示红牛似乎每个周末都会冒出一个新问题，此前他还开玩笑说，今年的种种挫折会让他在冬休期去西藏当个佛陀。
维斯塔潘表示，在匈牙利他受“赛车退化”的影响比轮胎退化更大，这是红牛需要解决的问题。
更严肃地说，维斯塔潘表示红牛需要控制住这类问题，尤其是在他在匈牙利经历了他所说的“赛车退化”之后——赛车在一个周末的进程中、甚至在一节练习中越跑越差。
“我们首先需要找到更多整体性能。然后我们需要解决我们的问题，也就是我们有时会在一个周末中损失性能，甚至从比赛开始到结束都在损失，”维斯塔潘说。
“所以，是的，那实际上是一个首要任务。”
维斯塔潘可以用一个词来概括2026赛季上半程：“艰难。”
“总的来说，非常艰难。有一些好时刻，一些我想是闪亮的时刻，但总体而言，一直很艰难。所以，我认为我们需要努力变得更稳定、更全面一些，让周末更顺利。此外，我们还需要找到更多性能。
“归根结底就这么简单。然后，除了找到更多性能之外，就是不要让现有套件出现这些问题。”
红牛也仍在与入弯不稳定和弯中转向不足作斗争。
皮埃尔·瓦什指出小红牛22的两个弱点
虽然维斯塔潘强调红牛需要防止这些负面意外，但技术总监皮埃尔·瓦什承认，小红牛22还存在几位车手都抱怨过的几个具体问题。
“我认为，就像每辆赛车一样，你会看到车手使用赛车的方式、其载荷，以及在平衡和尝试重新平衡赛车方面所能做的特性上存在一些局限。
“显然，我们像每辆赛车一样，在入弯稳定性和弯中转向不足方面存在一些局限。我们尝试通过使用一些机械手段来避免这些方面，”瓦什在接受Autosport采访时说。
维斯塔潘非常不喜欢弯中转向不足，不过红牛两位车手在这方面的反馈相当相似。
当Autosport问哈贾尔他认为最大的局限是什么时，他指出了与瓦什相同的方面。
“入弯稳定性需要解决，然后我们才能改进其余部分，”这位21岁的法国车手说。
尽管存在这些问题，红牛自赛季初的艰难阶段以来已取得显著进步。瓦什在回顾2026赛季开局那几个痛苦的比赛周末时也得出了同样的结论。
“关于赛车一开始的问题，显然相比其他一些人我们缺少一些载荷。而且我们赛车上还有一些机械小毛病，导致车手通过方向盘感觉不到赛车。我们在初期纠正了这一点。
“这花了一点时间，但它叠加在整体性能[不足]和赛车潜力之上。所以是的，我们在车手感觉方面有一些问题，这不是秘密。”
detailEn: Verstappen highlights "big priority" for Red Bull in second half of F1 2026
Max Verstappen says Red Bull urgently needs to understand why its car sometimes gets worse over the course of an F1 weekend. Technical director Pierre Wache points to another weakness
During Formula 1's summer break, Max Verstappen finds himself no fewer than 110 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

Last season, the four-time world champion launched a spectacular comeback from Zandvoort onwards and finished on the podium in every grand prix during the second half of the season, but this time he is absolutely not expecting that scenario.

Red Bull's problems are more complex this time around. The team started the season with a significant deficit, which had been expected, albeit for different reasons. Before the season, its own power unit was the biggest question mark, although the DM01 has proved surprisingly competitive.

On the chassis side, however, the shortcomings were greater. Add the RB22's excess weight to the equation and it becomes clear why Red Bull was more than 1.3 seconds off in terms of pure race pace in Australia and China, according to figures from Paceteq.
That gap had been reduced to two tenths per lap in Belgium and Hungary, although Verstappen believes those figures do not tell the whole story.

In Budapest, the Dutchman said that a new problem seems to emerge at Red Bull every weekend, having previously joked that all the setbacks this year would lead him to spend the winter break as a Buddha in Tibet.
Verstappen says that in Hungary he was more affected by "car degradation" than tyre degradation, an issue Red Bull needs to address

On a more serious note, Verstappen says Red Bull needs to get these kinds of issues under control, particularly after he experienced what he described as "car degradation" in Hungary, with the car getting worse over the course of the weekend and even during a session.

"We need to first find more overall performance. And then we need to fix our problems, where we sometimes just lose performance over a weekend, or even from the start of the race to the end,” Verstappen said.
"So, yeah, that is actually a big priority."
Verstappen can sum up the first half of the 2026 season in one word: "Tough."

"In general, it’s been very tough. Some good moments, some bright and shining moments, I guess, but in overall, it has been tough. So, I think we need to try and be more solid, a bit more all-round, to have more straightforward weekends. Plus, we need to find more performance.
"It’s as simple as that at the end of the day. Then, besides finding more performance, just not having these issues with the current package."
Red Bull is also still struggling with corner entry instability and mid-corner understeer
Pierre Wache identifies two weaknesses of the RB22

While Verstappen stresses that Red Bull needs to prevent these negative surprises, technical director Pierre Wache acknowledges that the RB22 also has several specific problems that both drivers have complained about.

"I think, as with every racing car, you see some limitations in how the drivers can use the car, the load of it, and the characteristics of what you can do in terms of balance and trying to rebalance the car.

"Clearly, we have some limitations, like every racing car, in terms of stability on [corner] entry and mid-corner understeer. And we try to avoid those aspects by using some mechanical tools to achieve it," Wache said when asked by Autosport.
Verstappen strongly dislikes mid-corner understeer, although the feedback from both Red Bull drivers is fairly similar in that respect.
When Autosport asked Hadjar what he considers the biggest limitation, he pointed to the same areas as Wache.
"Entry stability needs to be solved, and then we can improve the rest," the 21-year-old French driver said.

Despite these problems, Red Bull has made significant progress since the difficult opening phase of the season. Wache reaches the same conclusion when reflecting on the painful opening race weekends of 2026.

"Regarding the issues with the car at the beginning, clearly we were missing some load compared to some others. And we also had some mechanical gremlins on the car, which meant the driver didn’t feel the car through the steering. We corrected that at the beginning.
"It took a little bit of time, but it came on top of the overall performance [deficit] and the potential of the car. So yeah, we had some issues with the drivers’ feeling, that is not a secret."

detailZh: F1卡塔尔大奖赛：乔治·拉塞尔击败安东内利夺得杆位
乔治·拉塞尔在2026年第六次夺得杆位，梅赛德斯车队在F1卡塔尔大奖赛的预赛中全面领先。
乔治·拉塞尔在F1卡塔尔大奖赛中夺得杆位，击败队友安东内利，梅赛德斯车队在多哈的比赛中全面领先。
在卢塞尔赛道的高下压力赛道上，梅赛德斯车队在周末的每一节练习中都证明了自己比竞争对手更胜一筹，并通过利用其转向优势锁定了前两排。
拉塞尔在决定性的Q3冲刺赛中，在第一轮和第二轮中分别跑出1m21.695s的成绩，领先他的世界冠军队友近两十分，并且明显领先其他竞争者。
安东内利质疑自己为何在最后一轮中排在第一位，这位意大利少年在第二次尝试中找不到任何改进，最终排名第二。拉塞尔几乎复制了他的第一次成绩，但无需改进就赢得了他本赛季第六个杆位，这对于他的成长之旅意义重大。
迈凯轮的兰多·诺里斯在第二轮中提高了十分，以第三名的成绩领先队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，而伊萨克·哈吉亚在排位赛中击败了他的红牛队友马克斯·维斯塔潘，获得了第五个发车位。
法拉利在多哈的糟糕周末继续，整个练习赛中都在为抓地力和速度而挣扎。查尔斯·勒克莱尔只能排在第七位，距离杆位有1.260秒的差距。青训车队小红牛的菜鸟车手阿维德·林德布拉德击败了刘易斯·汉密尔顿的第二辆法拉利，利亚姆·劳森以第十名的成绩结束了前十。
红牛车队在Q2的表现与梅赛德斯车队相当接近，哈德贾的成绩为1m22.344s，比领跑者拉塞尔慢不到三十分之一，拉塞尔以1m22.079s的成绩领先安东内利。
在这两支车队和梅赛德斯车队之后，法拉利再次陷入困境，勒克莱尔落后整整一秒，他们试图与小红牛车队抗衡。
尽管如此，两队仍有足够的余地进入Q3。对于前十名的争夺，哈斯、阿尔派和奥迪之间的竞争非常激烈，但最终这三支车队都没有足够的实力去威胁排名第十的劳森。
奥利弗·贝尔曼最接近，只差0.240s未能晋级。皮埃尔·加斯利从FP2中失去的时间中恢复过来，在发车位上获得第十二名，随后是加布里埃尔·博托莱托和他的队友弗朗哥·科拉平托。哈斯车队的新人拉斐尔·卡马拉和经验丰富的尼科·胡肯伯格将在周日的第八排发车。
梅赛德斯和红牛是唯一两支在Q1中只完成了一圈计时圈速的车队，拉塞尔的1分22.557秒领先，排在安东内利和维斯塔潘之前。其他领跑者虽然也在磨损的轮胎上完成了一圈，但同样也为稍后保留了关键的软胎。
第一轮练习结束后，卡洛斯·塞恩斯和亚历克斯·阿隆诺在圈外观望，威廉姆斯车手在第二轮练习后仍保持在这个位置。这对科拉平托来说是个安慰，他凭借0.1秒的优势从第16位惊险晋级Q1。与此同时，哈斯车队的新人卡马拉也晋级到第14位，但他为此不得不使用第二套软胎。
费尔南多·阿隆索和兰斯·斯特罗尔分别以第19位和第20位为陷入困境的阿斯顿·马丁车队挣扎，凯迪拉克车队的瓦尔特里·博塔斯和塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯完成了周日的排位赛。
detailEn: F1 Qatar GP: George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole
George Russell takes sixth pole of 2026 as Mercedes dominates qualifying at Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix
George Russell has grabbed an emphatic pole for Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix, defeating team-mate Kimi Antonelli as Mercedes blitzed the competition in Doha.

On the demanding, high-downforce circuit of Lusail, Mercedes proved a step ahead of the competition in every session over the weekend, and the Silver Arrows capitalised on their cornering advantage by locking out the front row.
Russell led from Antonelli after the first of two runs in the decisive Q3 shootout with a 1m21.695s lap, nearly two tenths up on his world champion team-mate and well clear of the competition.

As Antonelli questioned being out first in the queue for the final runs, the Italian teenager struggled to find any improvement on his second attempt and settled for second. Russell almost matched his first run, but did not need to improve to claim his sixth pole of a character-building campaign.
McLaren's Lando Norris found a tenth on his second lap to claim third ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri, with Isack Hadjar out-qualifying his Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen for fifth on the grid.

Ferrari continued a woeful weekend in Doha, having been struggling for grip and pace throughout practice. Charles Leclerc could only manage seventh on the grid, a shocking 1.260s off pole. Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad beat the second Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton to eighth, with Liam Lawson rounding out the top 10.
Red Bull, rather than McLaren, looked somewhat close to Mercedes in Q2, with Hadjar's 1m22.344s less than three tenths behind pacesetter Russell, who had the edge on Antonelli with a 1m22.079s lap.
Behind those two teams and McLaren, Ferrari struggled again, with Leclerc a full second behind as they looked to fight with Racing Bulls.

There was still a big enough cushion for both teams to make it into Q3, though. The battle for the top-10 was a tight fight between Haas, Alpine and Audi, but ultimately none of the three teams had enough in the tank to bother 10th-placed Lawson.

Oliver Bearman came closest, missing the cut by 0.240s. Pierre Gasly recovered from lost track time in FP2 to take 12th on the grid, followed by Gabriel Bortoleto and team-mate Franco Colapinto. Haas rookie Rafael Camara and veteran Nico Hulkenberg will start from the eighth row on Sunday.

Mercedes and Red Bull were the only two teams to just set one timed lap in Q1, with Russell's 1m22.557s leading the way ahead of Antonelli and Verstappen. The other frontrunners set a second time on scrubbed tyres, though, equally saving crucial sets of softs for later on.

After the first set of runs, Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon were on the outside looking in and the Williams drivers stayed in those positions after the second effort. That was a relief for Colapinto, who escaped Q1 by a tenth of a second in 16th. Meanwhile, Haas rookie Camara also advanced in 14th, but had to deploy a second set of softs to do so in 14th.
Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll were 19th and 20th for struggling Aston Martin, with Cadillac duo Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez completing Sunday's grid.

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.
